newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Asia-Pacific urge restraint on trade sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Asia-Pacific urge restraint on trade sanctions.

text.p: Top Asia-Pacific business leaders on Thursday urged APEC economies to refrain from using unilateral sanctions as a weapon in trade wars, warning these might restrict investment flows in the region.

Leaders of the APEC Business Advisory Council (ABAC) issued the call in a paper presented to Philippine President Fidel Ramos who will chair next month's summit of 18 member economies of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

"We call on APEC economies to limit the use of unilateral sanctions in connection with trade disputes, and to renounce the imposition of unilateral sanctions by an APEC member economy against any other member economy for non-trade purposes," they said in their paper.
"Use of such sanctions has the potential for restricting and distorting investment flows within APEC," they added.
At a news conference, ABAC chairman Roberto Romulo declined to say if this was targeted at the United States, which has alarmed some Asian nations with its use of sanctions.
The ABAC paper contained a series of recommendations for boosting trade and providing greater access to investment capital.

If U.S. President Bill Clinton and the other heads of government meeting at Subic Bay north of Manila accept the ABAC proposals, they could be incorporated in an APEC action agenda to be announced at the end of the summit.

APEC members include Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Taiwan, Thailand, Singapore and the United States.
